reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in transforming static pace extrapolation into dynamic probabilistic forecasting. Traditional methods fail because they assume constant speed, ignoring physiological fatigue and environmental variability. The proposed Bayesian framework introduces prior distributions over regression parameters, allowing for uncertainty propagation through posterior inference. This enables real-time updating of finish time expectations as new splits arrive. Quantile regression complements this by providing direct access to conditional quantiles without assuming normality. Both methods leverage multi-slice data—total pace and recent 5K pace—to enhance predictive fidelity. The failure mode occurs when splits are sparse or inconsistent, leading to unreliable parameter estimates. The dual nature of these primitives reflects the need for both probabilistic confidence and quantified risk bounds in high-stakes scenarios such as marathon racing.
